key_insight: Rigorous bounds establish O(N⁻¹) ground-energy basis error for plane-wave and spatial-grid quantum chemistry simulations, with comparable scaling for important observables.
engineering_relevance: These bounds help quantum algorithm designers choose basis sizes to meet energy and observable accuracy targets.
method: Bound ground-energy errors for plane-wave bases and spatial grids with periodic or open boundaries.
Analyze time-evolution errors in smoothed position observables and particle kinetic energy.
Separate open-boundary leakage error from discretization-resolution error.
evidence_signal: Analytical results give smoothed-position error O(N⁻⁵ᐟ³ + tN⁻¹) and kinetic-energy error O((t + log N)/N), where N is basis size and t is evolution time.
watch_item: Full-state evolution has a weaker error bound; open-boundary grids also require negligible leakage beyond the simulation domain.
paper_title: Basis-set error bounds for first-quantised quantum simulation of chemistry
